bling in the abdomen after every meal. Rumbling in the
abdomen, as from emptiness. Frequent accumulation of
flatulence in the abdomen. Incarceration of flatulence.
Creeping sensation in the right side of the abdomen, as if
he had taken a cathartic.

sections.label: Stool
sections.text:
Retention of stool. Frequent desire for stool.
Unsuccessful desire for stool. Sudden desire for stool,
the stool being first natural, then papescent, lastly thin,
with shuddering through the body from above downward,
and a drawing extending from the small of the back through
the thighs ; when about to rise, he feels all the time as if
he had not yet got through. Renewed desire for stool,
shortly after stool. Frequent desire for stool, passing
but little, and sometimes only mucus. Cosliveness for
a time. Dry stool in lumps. Dry stool of large size,
with violent cutting pains. Discharge of a single hard
lump with pressing. Difficult expulsion of tight, but
not hard stool, as if the bowels had not strength enough
to expel it, (a. 24 h.) Hard stool, which felt slippery
without being so. Loose stool in the forenoon, thin in the
afternoon. Frequent and continuous desire as if diarrhoea
would set in, in the evening, with pinching and painful
motion in the abdomen, as if caused by a cold, and with
shocks in the left side as from a felus, with distension of
the abdomen ; afterwards thin stool with desire remaining

STAXNUH.

after it, and colic continuing until she wer.t to bed. Stool
with mucus shaped as a worm. Greenish, scanty stool.
Soreness and smart ing in lite anus, will) fine slinging.
Burning pain in the region of i lie liver after stool. Dull
pressure in llie reclum after stool. Discharge of mucus
after stool. Burning at the anus, between and immedi-
ately afier stool. Aclnng pain in the reclum. Itching
stile!, in the rectum. Continual itching around the anus.
Liule blotch on the left side of the anus, resembling a
varix and sore to the touch. Corrosive pain round the
anus, when walkmg or sitting.

Urinary Organs. Retention of urine. Desire to

urinate, as if the bladder were full ; the urine being scanty,
fetid, the emissions being rare and painless. Frequent
desire to urinate, also at night, for three days ; after this
he urinated less than before taking 1 he drug. After mic-
turilion, intensely painful pressure in the nccU of the blad-
der and along the urethra; constant sensation as if urine
■were yet to come ; if some drops do come the pressure
becomes much worse. Burning m the forepart of the ure-
thra, especially when urinating ; he had a desire every
minute and emitted a good deal of urine. Vesicle on the
margin of the orifice of the urelhra. Soreness of the tip
of the urethra. Jerking in the penis, as far as the point of
insertion in the bladder, as if an emission would take place.

Genital Organs. — Burning in the interior of the geni-
tal organs, like a violent desire for an emission, (a. 24 h.)
No desire or power, not even when excited, (sec. cff.7)
Intolerable voluptuous feeling in the genital organs and in
the whole body, terminating in emission, (a. 40 h.) Burn-
ing pain in the glans, and shortly after desire to urinate.
Burning stitch in I he glans. Pricking sensation in the
glans. Erection, immediately ; no erection whatsoever the
three days following. Emissions, -without any dreams.
Prolapsus vaginae which is very inconvenient during hard

sections.label: stool
sections.text:
Pressing in the hypogastrium, as if the menses
would make their appearance ; worse when pressing upon
the parts. The menses are more profuse than usual, (12.
d.) Great anguish and melancholy the week previous to
the menses ; lltey cease as soon as the n»enses made their
appearance. Pain in the region of the malar bone pre?

BTANNDM.

240

vious to the menses, when touching it ; during the menses
conlusive pain in the region of the malar bone, it is felt
even when moving the muscles of the face. Discharge of
translucent mucus from the vagina. Cessation of the leu-
corrhoeal discharge.

Cold, Catarrh. — Frequent sneezing. Violent dry
coryza ; can breathe only through the right nostril ; the
nose becomes free on the fourth day. Obstruction of the
left nostril ; it is swollen externally, red and painful when
touched. Violent coryza, (a. 4 d.)

Larynx, Trachea and Chest. — Roughlhroat. Hoarse-
ness ; weakness and emptiness in the chest, when begin-
ning to sing, she had to interrupt herself continually and
to breathe ; the hoarseness was sometimes momentarily
relieved by a fit of cough. Mucus in the trachea, in the
forenoon, easily thrown off by a slight cough, the chest
feeling very weak as if deadened all over, with faintness
of ihe whole body and limbs, in which a weak feeling is
moving up and down ; many mornings in succession. Ac-
cumulation of mucus in the chest, with rattling breathing,
which can be felt internally, and heard by others. Titil-
lating creeping in the throat, (larynx ?) with a feeling of
dryness, obliging one to cough. Irritation in the trachea,
during an inspiration, as if from mucus, there being neither
mucus nor dry cough ; it is more violently felt when sit-
ting crooked than when walking. Short cough from lime
to time, as if from weakness of the chest, with hoarse,
weak sound. Short and hacking cough, three short fits.
Constant desire to cough as if owing to much mucus in
the chest, with an internal feeling of panting and slight
rattling. Constant desire to cough, from a continual con-
striction of the trachea. Titillating cough, as if from a
soreness deep in the trachea, with scratching rising up into
the throat. Exhausting fits of cough, which produced a
bru-sed sort of pain in ihe pit of the stomach. Oppression
ot the chest when coughing. Scraping throat, with green-
ish expectoration of a disagreeably sweetish taste, more
violent in the evening before going'lo bed ; hoarse speech ;
after every cough, (with irritation in the lower part of the
trachea,) sore feeling in the chest and trachea. Horrid
cough with expectoration and spitting of blood. Yellow

244


discharge from the trachea, having a putrid taste. Expec-
toration having a salt taste. Fit of asthma, short breath-
ing and anguish, in the evening. The breathing becomes
shorter in the evening, accompanied with anguish ; he is
obliged to breathe hurriedly for a long time until he
succeeds in drawing deep breath, when the shortness
disappears. Asthma and ivant of breathing, when go-
going up stairs and when performing the least motion.
Asthma as if the clothes were too tight ; he has to open
them, to breathe easily. Oppressive weight in the upper
part of the chest ; he is frequently obliged to take deep
breath, accompanied with a feeling of great emptiness in
the pit of the stomach. Oppression of the chest, as if
something were rising into the throat arresting the breath-
ing. Feeling of pleasant lightness when taking deep
breath, frequently. Feeling as if the chest expanded,
when at rest and occasionally, accompanied, however,
with a feeling of anxiety as in palpitation of the heart.
Short, troublesome breathing from weakness of the respi-
ratory organs, with great emptiness of the chest, but with-
out want of breathing. Oppression of the chest, as if
contracted internally, with sensation as if the inspired air
were very dry. Oppressive clawing in the chest, when
sitting ; increased by taking breath. Pressure deep in the
chest, as of a load. Tension and pressure across the up-
per part of the chest, in the morning when rising from the
bed. Constriction of the chest, in the evening, with an-
guish. Contractive pain in the chest under the right arm ;
becoming pricking when moving about. Stitches in the
chest and the should-er-jomt when taking breath. Violent
stitches in the chest and sides, hindering breathing, several
forenoons ; distension of the abdomen in the afternoon.
Tensive stitch in the sternum, continuing while taking
breath. A sudden long stitch in the left side of the chest,
one hand's breadth below the axilla, causing one to start.
Sudden sharp cuttings as with a knife, in the left side of
the chest. Sharp, piercing prickings on the clavicle. Fre-
quent cuttings through the chest from below upward, and
in front in the region of the upper ribs from within out-
ward, independent of breathing. Burning stitches in the
left side of the chest, more violent during an expiration,
when walking in the open air. Stitch, resembling a flea-


245

bite, in the last true rib of the right, and the false rib of the
left side. Lancinatioa in the left side of the chest, when
walking and standing. Cutting pain in the right chest.
Clawing cutting in the light ribs, when walking, only dur-
ing an inspiration. Pressure in the chest, below the right
nipple, from within outward. Aching in the whole chest,
especially above the pit of the stomach, worse during an
inspiration. Bruised pain in the chest, when at rest and
in motion. Sore pain in the whole chest, commencing in
the throat. Digging-up pain in the chest and thence de-
scending into the abdomen, exciting a desire for stool.
Drawing pressure in the region of the united cartilages of
the last false ribs. Drawing,, from the clavicles into the
left axilla. Sudden drawing under the left breast, when
raising one's self in the bed, followed by sharp cuttings
extending thence to the clavicle, in the direction of the
shoulder, where the pain remains fixed ; thence it moves
along the left shoulder into the abdomen, made worse when
drawing in the chest, pressing upon the part, and especially
during an inspiration and vomiturition ; in all these condi-
tions the pain is felt as a painful jerk. Jactitation of the
muscles of the upper part of the chest, near the left axilla.
Violent itching of the nipple.

sections.label: Back
sections.text:
Violent creeping in the small of the back.
Twitching jerking of the muscles of the last false ribs.
Burning pressure in the small of the back, a little to the
right. Painful pressure in the left side of the back above
the hip, from above downward. Undulating shock in the
back above the left ilium, causing him to start. Stitching
pinching in the back, in the region of the false ribs. Vio-
lent tearing in the lumbar vertebrae, extending from both
sides to the lumbar region, more violent at every move-
ment of the trunk. Dull shocks in the lumbar region,
with sensation as if a coolness were blowing upon him.
Sharp, jerking stitch in the left side of the back and at the
same time in the left thigh. Burning fine pricking in a
small spot of the middle of the back. Fine prickino-
through the back from within outward. Digging-up
stitches in the muscles of the right side of the back, con-
tinuing while taking breath. Lancination in the left side
of the back, from below upward, when standing. Draw-

246

BTANNUM.

ing pressure in the spine, below and between the scapulae,
more violent during motion, especially when turning the
body. When lifting a load she suddenly fell a sensation
between the scapulae as if sprained, more on ihe left side,
accompanied with violent sharp cuttings when making the
least motion, taking breath or yawning; when bending
backward she feels intolerable pains. Drawing tearing in
the left scapula, partly towards the back, partly towards
the shoulder. Slow, intermittent dull stitches between
the scapulas, towards the middle of the spine. Sharp broad
stitches in the spine, between the scapulae, from within
outward. Violent burning pricking in the upper part of
the scapula, going off only /or a short while by rubbing.
Burning pricking in the top of the right shoulder.

sections.label: Neck
sections.text:
Itching prickings in" the nape of the neck, in
the morning when in bed. Boring dull stitches from the
fauces through the muscles of the nape of the neck.
Drawing in the nape of the neck from below upward, with
a feeling of stiffness, she was not able to move her head
easily. Pain in the nape of the neck when bending the
head forward. Sudden intensely painful stitch in the
lower part of the nape of the neck. Weakness of the
muscles of the nape of the neck, as if she were not able
to support her head, with pain when moving the head.
Cracking of the cervical vertebrae, which can be even heard
by others, when shaking the head quickly. Red, somewhat
elevated spot on the fore part of the neck, with a white
painless pimple in the middle.

Upper Extremities. — Compressive sensation in the
shoulder. Tearing in the top of the left shoulder. Pres-
sure and drawing, as of a load, in the top of the left shoul-
der, in the outer parts of the upper arm, and likewise in
the deeper muscles of the fore-arm from the elbow, going
off gradually in the room. Paralytic tearing in and below
the right shoulder-joint, more violent during motion. Sud-
den, intensely painful, hard knocks on the right shoulder.
Itching prickings in and below the axilla. Paralytic pain
as if sprained, close below the shoulder-joint, only when
at. rest; going off only for a short while by motion.
Weariness in the arms and legs; he has to let his arms
hang down. Great debility in arms and legs, as if they

ITANNUM.

24T

had lost, all power, and as if the legs could not support the
bodv. Intensely painful jerking now in the surface of the
arm', now in that of the hand, now in a finger, resembling
a hard blow. Pain in the arm joints as if sprained ; she
was not able to bend them witlu ut great pain. Arms and
fingers arc almost entirely immoveable. Paralytic weak-
ness and oppressive weight of (he arms, especially tin
right arm, particularly of the upper arms and joints; aggra-
vated by every motion, and sometimes with want of breath.
Paralytic weakness in the arms, when holding a small
weight for a short time only. The arms become easily
fatigued by a slight effort, obliging him to let the things
which he holds in his hands drop. Paralytic tearing in
the left arm, especially the wrist-joint, more violent during
motion. Tearing deep in the left arm, especially the up-
per arm. Drawing in the left deltoid muscle, as from
weakness. Transitory drawing from the elbow towards
the upper arm. Tearing in the anterior and superior por-
tion of 1 he eight upper arm. Tearing, with pressure, in
the middle of the right upper arm, qnh'klv coming and
going. Tearing, with pressure, in the middle of the left
upper arm, from before backward and from without in-
ward. Tearing, with pressure in both upper arms, in
paroxysms. Jactitation of the muscles of the internal side
of the left upper arm, when laying thr> arm on someihing;
going off by changing the position of the arm, but return-
ing when the arm resumes its former position. Twitch-
ings in the muscles of the upper arm above the elbow-
joint, when at rest, (a. 5 and 2o" h.) Digging-up stitch in
the right deltoid muscle. Bruis.d pain in the lower part
of the left upper arm. Piercing pain, in paroxysms, in the
left humerus, as if crushed and compressed, when at rest
and in motion. Tension and sore feeling in the tip of the
elbow, especially when bending the arm. Cramp-like
stiffness in the right fore-arm. Paralytic tearing in the
right lower arm. Pressure in the light fore-arm, from be-
hind forward and from within outward. Pain as if sprain-
ed over the left wrist, in the region of the styloid process
of the ulna. Pain as if sprained in the left wrist-joint.
Tearing with pressure in the right wrist-joint, more v j-
lent during motion. Transitory jerking* in the dorsum of

248


l*ie. Ml jian(^' above the joint. Pinching close above the
wrist-joint, in the side of the ulna. Quick drawing, in
short paroxysms, from the ulnar side of the wrist-joint to-
wards the hand. Cramp-pain in the dorsum of the left
hand, between the index and middle-finger. Cramp-like
contraction of the palm of the left hand. Jerking tearing
in the hand, coming from the fingers. Tearing with pres-
sure, at intervals, in the metacarpal and carpal bones, and
also in the posterior joints of the fingers. Burning prick-
ing, with pressure, in the outer border of the metacarpal
bone coming from the left little finger. Fine, dull, in-
tensely painful shocks in the upper part of the metacarpal
bone of the left index-finger and in other parts of the
hands, as if a nerve, which had been put upon the stretch,
were touched with a little hammer. Weakness and tremb-
ling of the hands, especially when laying them upon the
table and writing, which gave him trouble. Trembling
and feeling of heat in the left hand. Swelling of the
hands, in the evening. Burning itching in the dorsum of
the hand, as if bit by mosquitoes, not to be removed by
rubbing, for eight hours. Small, red, painless spots on
the dorsa of both hands. Small blotches below the wrist ;
itching through the day, the itching being aggravated by
rubbing. Chilblains on the hand, during mild weather.
Tearing, with pressure in the posterior joints of the fingers
of the right hand, more violent during motion. Drawing
stitches in the posterior joint of the left index-finger, in
the direction of the tip. Cramp in the fingers, they remain
contracted for a long while. Cutting in the ball of the left
little finger, more violent when bending it forward. Prick-
ing in the tips of all the fingers. Fine prickings in the tip
of the left middle-finger. Drawing in the posterior joint
of the left thumb, and below the wrist. Cramp-like draw-
ing pain in the left middle-finger, with jerks causing the
finger to tremble. Intense jerking pain between the thumb
and index-finger, when holding the pen ; he does not feel
anything when holding the pen loose or ceasing to write,
but the jerking soon returns and continues a long while.
Tearing in the posterior joint of the index-finger, gradu-
ally going off when moving the hand. Pain of the whole
of the left index-finger as if sprained, when bending it,

STANNTJM.

249

stretching it, or when at rest, frequently recurring for five
days. Painful growing of the nails into the flesh.

Lower Extremities. — Continuous itching .pricking in
the left ham, near the anus. Jactitation of the left glutei
muscles. Violent pain in the muscles around the hip-
joint, when raising the thigh. Transitory dull pressure in
the ossa ischii, when sitting. Pain in the right hip as if
sprained, when walking, he was almost obliged to limp for
several hours. Drawing in the left hip. Paralytic pain
in the hip-joint when walking. Pain as if sprained close
below the hip-joint, in the thigh, only when walking. In-
quietude in the limbs, he has to change their position all
the time in the evening. Paralytic heaviness and toeak-
ness in the limbs, especially in the thighs and knee-joints ;
le is scarcely able to walk, but has lo sit and lie down.
Painful weariness of the lower limbs when standing, with
debility and staggering. Bruised pain of the lower limbs
when going up stairs ; when going down stairs they feel
so weak and powerless that he is in danger of falling.
Weakness of the right limb, especially the thigh, appa-
rently the femur; it pained him when standing, he had to
rest upon the left limb. Itching pricking in the upper
and inner side of the thigh. Stitch-like pain in the mus-
cles of the right thigh, only when standing. Pricking in
the inner side of the left thigh. Drawing with pressure,
on the inner side of the left thigh, in the groin, extending
from the os ischium to the posterior side of the thigh,
afterwards from the hip to above the small of the back
on the right side ; with occasional grumbling in the
os ischium. Cutting in the interior of the left thigh.
Pulsative dull pressure in the middle of the inner side of
the thigh. Pain as if sprained in the thigh, below the
hip-joint, when walking. Drawing tearing in the left
thigh, both when at rest and in motion. ' Drawing pres-
sure on the outer side of the right thigh, which he had laid
across the other when sitting. Pricking itching in the
outer side of the thigh, going off for a lime only by rub-
bing, (a. h h.) Itching pimple on the left thigh. Pres-
sure on the right knee-joint. Tensive pain in the bend of
the left knee. Stiffness in the bend of the right knee.
Sudden stiffness of the knee, she can only bend it with

250


great pain. Drawing tearing in the bone, from the knee
to the middle of the thigh, when silling. Tearing with
pressure in ihe right knee-joini, in front, from without
inward and below the patella. Tearing in the ligaments
of the internal side of the left knee. Burning scratching
in the outer side of the left knee. Dull sliiching in the
outer side of the right knee, only when standing; going off
again when moving the limb and when silting. Fine,
painful slilches in the right knee and bend of the knee,
when sitting. Fainlness in the knee joint, he is scarcely
able to walk, with drowsiness. Jerking iwitchings below
ihe patella. Bruised pain in the bends of the knees and
calves as after taking a long journey, in ihe evening, when at
rest and in motion. Cold knees and feet. Drawing tear-
ing in the leg, when sitting* Cramp-like tearing in the
right leg, when walking. Painful drawing in the outer
side of the calf, when at rest and in motion. Tension in
the left leg. Drawing, extending from the bend of ihe
right, knee to the calf. Great weariness of the legs, espe-
cially the left, extending from the feet upward and through
the knees with a jerk, especially when standing, with
soreness of the soles. When walking, especially when
walking in the sun, her knees threaten to bend, with faint-
ness of the whole body and faint sweat in the face. Pain-
ful rigid stiffness in the inner side of the lelt calf when
standing. Violent cramp in the calf, almost the whole
night. Pressure in the whole of the right calf. Pressure
below the right calf, when at rest and in motion. Pinch-
ing in the upper part of the inner muscles of the calf.
Frequent painful heaviness in the outer muscles of the
left calf, when walking. Sensation in the leg as if a cord
had been tied round firmly. Painful feeling of a heavy
weight in the left leg which he had laid across the other
when sitting, and which was hanging down. Pulsative
pressure in the right tibia. Yellow, round spots on the
left leg, for two days. Small swelling on the tibia, with a
red point on it ; when touching that point a pain is felt as
if the flesh were loose from the bone. Pain of the feet
from above the malleoli down to the soles, when sitting,
less when standing or walking. Disagreeable heat
in the feet, which can scarcely be felt by the hand.

STANNUH.

251

Violent burning in the feet and hands. Flush of heat in
the feet. Reddish swelling of the feet, especially around
the ankles, with sensation as if ihc feet were lied too fast*
Sudden swelling around the ankles, in the evening. Pain
under the ankles, in the evening when lying in the bed,
as if the heel were torn out. Tearing, with jerks, in both
ankles of the right foot, and thence into the toes when sit-
ting ; when standing die pain seems less, but then the
tearing is felt from the toes upward. Creeping in the
feel, as after a long walk, or as if they would go to sleep,
gradually rising into ihe legs. Itching pricking under the
left inner and outer ankle. Itching in the dorsum of the
left foot. Tearing with pressure in the right heel. Draw-
ing tearing between the metatarsal bones of the last two
toes. When treading on the outer side of the right heel,
a dull stitching pressure is felt as far as the calf, only when
walking ; disappearing when raising the foot. Cramp-
pain in the sole of the right foot, when silting. Sharp
pressure transversely across the right sole, when sitting.
Stitching pinching, alternately in various parts of the body.
Heavy pressure now in one, now in another bone.

General Symptoms. — Heaviness in all the limbs,
faintness in the chest and more or less violent fits of
anxiety. Bruised pain In ihe limbs, and especially above
the small of the back. Paralysis of the left arm and foot,
from fright, disappearing in the night. Internal heat after
a walk in the open air, especially in the chest and abdo-
men, without thirst. Itching burning pricking over the
whole body, especially in the outer parts of the trunk,
particularly in the morning when in bed, for some days.
Corrosive itching when undressing, over the whole body,
ho was obliged to scratch. Fine prickings in the whole
left side of the body, next day only in the right. Itching
eruption over the whole body. Many pains, especially the
drawing pains with pressure, commence lightly, increase
gradually and to a very high degree, and decrease again
as slowly. The symptoms seem to disappear when walk-
ing, they return immediately when at rest; the lassitude
is greatest when Walking. Causes consumption.

V\ e a k ness, Fits. — Extreme relaxation of body and
mind ; he is unable to attend to his work for a Ions time,

252

STAN NUM.

has to lie down and sleep. Loss of strength, as if his
lower limbs had been crushed. Excessive heaviness ;
he wants to sit or lie down, when sitting down he almost
falls down upon his chair, he has not strength enough to
sit down gradually. Great weariness with constant in-
clination to sit down ; he feels this weariness most when
walking slowly, and he therefore walks fast involuntarily.
He feels his weariness less when walking fast, but so much
more afterwards. Trembling and unsteady in the whole
body and limbs ; the hand trembles more when laying it
lightly upon something, than when grasping a thing firmly.
Weariness in the whole body for 7 days, especially after
going up-stairs. Great weariness in the day-time ; he has
to lie down, but he is unable to sleep ; and, if he does
sleep, he is attacked with vertigo, absence of mind, and
dulness, for half an hour. Faint and drowsy. Great
faintness after going down-stairs, she was scarcely able to
breathe, felt nothing when going up-stairs, (Real epilepsy.)

sections.label: Sleep
sections.text:
Stretching of the arms and leg. A good deal
of yawning when walking in the open air, but with oppres-
sion, as if a hoop were around the chest. Violent desire
to gape ; nevertheless he was not able to gape wide
enough even when opening the mouth ever so widely.
Drowsiness after a walk in the open air, especially when
hearing music Drowsiness in the evening ; sleep being
prevented by a constant impatience in the legs. Frequent
starting in the night, when asleep. Impatience in the
whole body, after waking at 1 o'clock in the night, with
digging-up in the tibiae. Deep sleep for several nights.
(He spoke during sleep and said that an external applica-
tion could not cure an internal affection.) The child
moans during the nightly sleep, prays and supplicates in
a timid manner. Vivid dreams. Anxious dreams, of
quarrels, neglected business. Confused, vivid dreams,
things do not succeed according to her wishes, she talks
aloud, tosses about, and, when waking, finds herself sit-
ting up. He hears a loud report in a dream. Pleasant
dream of earthly magnificence and greatness. Dream full
•of cruelty. Lascivious dream with emission, without erec-
tion. Lascivious dream with erection, without emission.
When waking, in the night, he lies on his back, with the


253

right limb stretched, and the left limb drawn up, and half
uncovered. In the night, after waking, undulating draw-
ing jerks deep in the hand, apparently in the nerves,
he could have exclaimed. Drowsy and dizzy in the morn-
ing, when waking from a long sleep, as if he had not slept
enough. In the morning, when waking, back and lower
limbs are painful as if bruised ; she feels tired as if she
had not slept enough and as if the body had not been
rested long enough ; she feels a little better a few hours after
rising. While dressing herself, she is suddenly attacked
with so much weakness that she is scarcely able to breathe.
In the morning when waking, he feels a pain and heat in
the head.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Shuddering, only in the left arm, it caused the
arm to jerk. Shuddering, in the evening, only in the left
foot, up to half the thigh. Shuddering, at 10 o'clock in
the forenoon, several days, with coldness of the hands,
deadness of the fingers and insensibility in the tips of the
fingers. Slight feeling of coldness and moderate shudder-
ing, with goose-flesh on the arms and continued chattering
of the teeth, resembling a convulsion of the masseter mus-
cles. Chilliness over the whole body, for half an hour.
Quickly passing chilliness, along the back especially.
Feeling of heat, especially internally. Great heat in the
head, with hot forehead, sometimes with redness of the
face, accompanied wilh a general, but slight heat of the
whole body, worse in the evening, with much thirst, five
evenings in succession, (a. 5 d.) Feeling of heat over the
whole body, especially on the thighs and the back. Violent
heat over the whole body, especially the chest and
back, with a feeling as of hot sweat trickling down, with-
out any heat being felt by the hand. He is now and then
attacked with anxious heat, as if sweat would break out.
Anxious heat and sweat set in all the time, even when

Sad and anxious. Discouraged. Dread of
seeing people.

Much adhesive mucus, difficult to de-
tach ; efforts to detach cause nausea. Throat dry and
stings.

sections.text:
Hunger. Smell of cooking causes vomit-
ing. Bitter taste. Pain better pressure, but sore to
touch. Sensation of emptiness in stomach.

Cramp-Uke colic around navel, with a
feeling of emptiness. Colic relieved hv hard pressure.

sections.text:
Bearing-down sensation. Prolapsus, with
weak, sinking feeling in stomach. [Sep.] Menses early
and profuse. Pain in vagina, upward and back to
spine. Leucorrhcea, with great debility.

Respiratory, — Hoaise, mucus expelled by forcible
cough. Violent, dry cough in evening until midnight.

sections.text:
Sleeps with one leg drawn up, the other
stretched out.

sections.label: Extremities
sections.text:
Paralytic weakness ; drpps things.
Ankles swollen. Limbs suddenly give out when at-
tempting to sit down. Dizziness and weakness when
descending. Spasmodic twitching of muscles of fore-
arm and hand. Fingers jerk when holding pen. Neu-
ritis. Typewriters’ paralysis.

sections.label: Fever
sections.text:
Heat in evening; exhausting night-sweats,
especially towards morning. Hectic. Perspiration, prin-
cipally on forehead and nape of neck ; debilitating ;
smelling musty, or offensive.

sections.label: Modalities
sections.text:
Worse, using voice (i. r., laughing, talk-
ing, singing), lying on right side, warm drinks. Better,
coughing or expectorating, hard pressure.

sections.label: Relationship

Complementary : Puls.

with tickling at root of tongue; stale of purulent in-
filtration) ; Caust.; Calc.; Sil.; Tuberc.; Bacil.; Melon.

phthisis, emphysema, with gastric catarrhal complica-
tions and thick, yellow^ difficult sputum. Old persons
with weakened power of expectoration).

sections.text:
Confusion and Vertigo. Confusion and dulness of the

* Gonstrieiion and sudden pressure in the tvhole upper part of the head, slowly

ished coryza (twelfth day),'*. — Blood is blown froRi the nose, in the morn-
